name: olympic-games

description.en: The host cities of all 55 Summer and Winter Olympic Games held from Athens 1896 to Milano Cortina 2026 (the Games cancelled in 1916, 1940 and 1944 and the 1906 Intercalated Games are not included). Front: the Games, e.g. "1912 Summer Olympics"; back: the host city in English and Swedish, both cities for the co-hosted 2026 Games, with a note where it helps (such as the 1956 equestrian events in Stockholm). Taken from Wikidata and checked against the IOC's list of Games (olympics.com) and Olympedia.
description.sv: Värdstäderna för alla 55 olympiska sommar- och vinterspel som hållits från Aten 1896 till Milano Cortina 2026 (de inställda spelen 1916, 1940 och 1944 och extraspelen i Aten 1906 ingår inte). Framsida: spelen, t.ex. ”Olympiska sommarspelen 1912”; baksida: värdstaden på engelska och svenska, båda städerna för spelen 2026, som hade två värdstäder, med en anteckning där den hjälper (som ridsporten i Stockholm 1956). Uppgifterna är hämtade från Wikidata och kontrollerade mot IOK:s lista över spelen (olympics.com) och Olympedia.

method: Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction. The deck was then cross-checked by independent AI reviewers (quality-control rounds 1–5: factual accuracy; language and translation; licensing, attribution and documentation; a final re-check of all cards and the documentation; a final full-deck review of facts and language), whose findings were verified and applied, and by machine checks against live Wikidata and the app's SHACL/DCAT-AP validators. The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.

Finding the Games in Wikidata: a first query (query 1) asked for items that are instances (P31) of Summer Olympic Games (Q159821) or Winter Olympic Games (Q82414) and returned nothing, because the editions are instances of edition classes (for example Q135976384 "Summer Olympic Games edition", as the entity API showed for the 1912 Games, Q8118, query 2). Query 3 instead selected every item whose P3450 (sports season of league or competition) is Q159821 or Q82414, with its start and end times (P580/P582), the truthy P276 (location) and P17 (country) values and the English and Swedish labels. The raw CSV was saved.

Selection: of the items from query 3, those with a start time (the Games actually held) from 1896 to 2026 became the cards: 30 Summer Games (1896–2024) and 25 Winter Games (1924–2026), 55 in all. The items for 1916, 1940 and 1944 (Summer) and 1940 and 1944 (Winter) have no start time: they were cancelled and are left out. Future Games (2028 onward) are left out. The 1906 Intercalated Games are not an edition of either series in Wikidata and are not counted by the IOC; they are left out (see the selection).

Host cities: the Games' P276 is not uniform. For 40 Games its truthy value includes the host city (sometimes with preferred rank and the qualifier "most precise value"). For 14 others the truthy values are venues only (for 1972 Summer the preferred value is the Olympic Stadium, which hides the normal-rank Munich). Query 4 listed every P276 statement of all ranks that is a human settlement, and query 5 every P276 statement (all ranks) of the Games without a city, with the venue's P131 (located in the administrative unit). For these 14 Games the city comes from the venue: e.g. 1952 Winter, Bislett Stadion (Q866409) located in Oslo Municipality (Q5245991), whose capital (P36) is Oslo (Q585); 1972 Winter, Makomanai Open Stadium (Q673240) in Minami-ku (Q1134027), itself in Sapporo (query 7). Each of these was also confirmed by an English alias of the Games item of the form "Oslo 1952" where Wikidata has one (queries 8 and 9). For 1960 Winter the preferred P276 is the ski resort Palisades Tahoe (Q2182804), whose English alias is "Squaw Valley"; the card gives the historical name Squaw Valley, used by the IOC and Olympedia.

English and Swedish names: the fronts are the Wikidata English and Swedish labels of the Games items, which follow one pattern ("1912 Summer Olympics" / "Olympiska sommarspelen 1912"). Query 6 fetched every English and Swedish label and alias of the host-city items. The English back is the city's English label or an alias that is the common short name (Chamonix rather than the commune name Chamonix-Mont-Blanc; Squaw Valley; Pyeongchang rather than Pyeongchang County; Lillehammer from the town item Q3745117, since the municipality item's Swedish label is "Lillehammers kommun"). The Swedish back is the Swedish label (Aten, Antwerpen, Helsingfors, Rom, München, Montréal, Moskva, Peking, Sankt Moritz, Saint Louis, Sotji, Turin, Milano …); for Oslo, which has no Swedish label, the multilingual (mul) label "Oslo". For the co-hosted 2026 Games the back names both cities, "Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo" / "Milano och Cortina d'Ampezzo".

Swedish check: the script fetch_games.py (query 9) fetched the Games items' labels, aliases and sitelinks and the introductions of their Swedish and English Wikipedia articles through the MediaWiki API. Every card's Swedish city name was found in the first sentence of the Swedish article that names the host city ("… hölls i Helsingfors i Finland …"); that sentence is quoted in the card's evidence. In quality-control round 3 every quoted Wikipedia introduction was fetched again with its revision id (query 21): the 62 quotes checked by revids.py were still verbatim, the two others (the Pyeongchang introduction, query 20, and the 1956 quarantine sentence) were checked against their own revisions, and each locator now links its revision. In round 4 all 64 quotes were checked again against the linked revisions (query 24) and all were verbatim; the Chamonix quote added in round 4 comes from query 23.

Cross-check against the IOC: the list of Games on olympics.com could not be fetched from the research environment (connections timed out, query 10), so the Internet Archive's capture of 2026-09-23 was downloaded (query 11) and the edition names in its page data were extracted; every card's city matched the IOC's name for the edition ("Stockholm 1912", "Turin 2006", "PyeongChang 2018", "Milano Cortina 2026" …). The IOC's Melbourne 1956 page (capture of 2026-01-13, query 12) was read for the equestrian events in Stockholm.

Cross-check against Olympedia: the Games overview (query 13) gives each edition's city, dates and status. All 55 cities agree with the cards (Olympedia writes local forms such as Athina, Roma, München, Torino and "Milano-Cortina d'Ampezzo"). It lists the 1956 equestrian Games in Stockholm in a separate row (10–17 June), the 1916, 1940 and 1944 Games as "Not held due to war", and the 1906 Games in a separate "Intercalated Games" table.

Notes: a back note was written, in the compiler's own words, only where it helps to answer or to avoid a wrong answer: the 1956 equestrian events in Stockholm, Tokyo 2020 held in 2021, the commune name Chamonix-Mont-Blanc, the present names of Squaw Valley, Sarajevo then in Yugoslavia, the Italian name Torino, Pyeongchang County and the IOC's spelling, and the official name and other sites of Milano Cortina 2026. Each note's facts were checked against Wikidata and the English (for Pyeongchang also the Swedish) Wikipedia introduction (for 1924 the introduction of the article on Chamonix, and Wikidata's official name, P1448, of Q83236), and the 1956 note also against the IOC and Olympedia. Two notes give a reason that is not in a Wikidata label or main value: the 1956 quarantine rules for horses (IOC Melbourne 1956 page and the English Wikipedia; Wikidata gives only the June 1956 equestrian qualifiers on the Stockholm location) and the 2020 postponement (also recorded in Wikidata's P580 qualifiers).

Machine checks: for every card the builder checks against live Wikidata the English and Swedish labels of the Games (the front), the P276 link from the Games to the city or venue, the P131 chain from the venue to the city where needed, an English alias of the Games naming the city where one exists, and the English and Swedish labels or aliases of the city (the back); for Turin also the Italian label "Torino" given in the note. The builder accepts a multilingual (mul) label for any language, so a check on a language the item lacks (Oslo, Q585, has no sv label) passes on the mul label; the evidence says where that happens. The deck was then validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (scripts/validate_sources.ts).
selection: All Olympic Games actually held, Summer and Winter, from the first modern Games (Athens 1896) to the most recent (Milano Cortina, February 2026): 30 Summer and 25 Winter Games. Left out: the Games cancelled because of the world wars (Summer 1916, 1940, 1944; Winter 1940, 1944), which were awarded but never held; the 1906 Intercalated Games in Athens, which the IOC does not count as Olympic Games (it is not in the IOC's list of editions, and Olympedia lists it apart from the Olympic Games); future Games (Los Angeles 2028 onward); the Youth Olympic Games, the Paralympic Games and the 1956 equestrian Games as a card of their own (they are part of the 1956 Summer Olympics and appear in that card's note). The back gives the host city, not the country or the venues; where events were spread over several places, the back names the host city the IOC names the Games after.
licensing: The only content source is Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0: the selection of Games, the English and Swedish names of the Games and of the host cities, and the link from each Games to its host city all come from it, so the deck can be CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. The IOC's olympics.com and Olympedia (both all rights reserved) and the English and Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only: they confirmed facts the Wikidata data gave and supplied, as uncopyrightable facts restated in the compiler's own words, the reasons given in two notes (the 1956 quarantine rules for horses, from the IOC and the English Wikipedia; the 2020 postponement, which Wikidata also records); no wording, table or selection was copied from them. The selection is every held edition of two Wikidata series, which coincides with any complete list of Olympic Games because it is the complete set, not a choice taken from a list; the notes are the compiler's own wording of facts, and facts are not copyrightable. Quotations in the provenance report's evidence are not part of the CC0 deck: they remain under their sources' licences (Wikipedia text CC BY-SA 4.0, by Wikipedia contributors, each linked to the quoted revision; the IOC's text all rights reserved) and are short quotations given only to make the verification checkable.

rounds.lens: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's host city against Wikidata, the IOC's list of editions and Olympedia; the Swedish names against Wikidata labels and the Swedish Wikipedia; the notes against Wikidata and the English Wikipedia.
rounds.scope: All 55 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.
rounds.summary: Wikidata, the IOC and Olympedia agree on the host city of all 55 Games; no card follows a value that a better source contradicts, and no Wikidata check was skipped. The discrepancies are in how Wikidata models the location (14 Games have only venues as truthy P276 values, 1960's preferred P276 is the ski resort under its present name, 1956 has Stockholm as a second, normal-rank location), handled by checking the venue's P131 chain and an alias of the Games. Builder checks cover the front labels, the Games-to-city link and the back labels of every card.

findings.issue: Wikidata P276 has Melbourne (preferred) and Stockholm (normal rank); the equestrian events were held in Stockholm in June 1956. Naming both cities on the back would make the Games look co-hosted, which the IOC and Olympedia do not do.
findings.resolution: Back Melbourne (the IOC's Melbourne 1956); the note says the equestrian events were held in Stockholm in June 1956 because of Australia's quarantine rules for horses (IOC Melbourne 1956 page; Olympedia's separate Equestrian row, 10–17 June). The builder checks only the truthy (preferred) Melbourne value.

findings.issue: Wikidata's preferred P276 is Palisades Tahoe (Q2182804), the ski resort's present name; a normal-rank P276 is Olympic Valley (Q822230), the community's present name; a deprecated P276 is Yokuts Valley (Q2141628), a different place in Fresno County formerly also called Squaw Valley. The IOC and Olympedia call the Games Squaw Valley 1960.
findings.resolution: Back "Squaw Valley" (the name of the place in 1960, an alias of both Wikidata items, and the IOC's and Olympedia's name); the note gives the present names. Checks: P276 Q2182804, its alias "Squaw Valley", Q822230's English and Swedish alias "Squaw Valley" and the Games' alias "Squaw Valley 1960".

findings.issue: Wikidata's English and Swedish labels of the host commune are "Chamonix-Mont-Blanc"; the IOC ("Chamonix 1924") and Olympedia ("Chamonix") use the short name.
findings.resolution: Back "Chamonix" (an English and Swedish alias in Wikidata); the note gives the commune's official name.

findings.issue: Wikidata's P276 for the 1952 Winter Games is only Bislett Stadion, located in Oslo Municipality (Q5245991), not the city item Oslo (Q585), which has no Swedish label (only the multilingual label "Oslo").
findings.resolution: Back Oslo; checks P276 Bislett Stadion, its P131 Oslo Municipality, the Games' alias "Oslo 1952" and Q585's labels (the builder accepts the mul label for Swedish). Same approach (venue P131 plus Games alias) for 1964 Winter, 1972 Summer and Winter, 1984 Summer and Winter, 1988 Summer, 1992, 1994, 1998, 2002, 2006, 2010 and 2018 Winter.

findings.issue: The venue chain ends at Lillehammer Municipality (Q101341), whose Swedish label is "Lillehammers kommun".
findings.resolution: Back Lillehammer, with the label checks on the town item Q3745117 (English and Swedish label "Lillehammer").

findings.issue: The venue chain ends at Pyeongchang County (Q188624, English label "Pyeongchang County"); the IOC writes "PyeongChang 2018".
findings.resolution: Back "Pyeongchang" (English alias and Swedish label of Q188624, the Swedish Wikipedia's form); the note says it is Pyeongchang County and gives the IOC's spelling.

findings.issue: Wikidata's start time is 2021-07-24; Olympedia, the English and Swedish Wikipedia give the opening as 23 July 2021 (some events from 21 July). The front says 2020 but the Games were held in 2021.
findings.resolution: The card gives no day; the note says the Games were postponed by a year and held in July and August 2021, still as Tokyo 2020. Check P580 year 2021.

findings.issue: The Games were officially co-hosted; Wikidata's P276 also lists other venues (Verona, Bormio, Livigno, Predazzo, Tesero …). The IOC calls them "Milano Cortina 2026", Olympedia "Milano-Cortina d'Ampezzo".
findings.resolution: Back names both host cities, "Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo" / "Milano och Cortina d'Ampezzo"; the note gives the official name and says events were also held elsewhere in northern Italy.

findings.issue: Swedish forms of St. Louis vary (Wikidata sv label "Saint Louis", aliases "S:t Louis", "St. Louis").
findings.resolution: Swedish back "Saint Louis", the Wikidata Swedish label and the form in the Swedish Wikipedia's article on the 1904 Games ("hölls i Saint Louis i USA").

findings.issue: olympics.com could not be reached from the research environment (HTTP/2 stream errors and timeouts).
findings.resolution: The IOC pages were read from the Internet Archive's captures of 2026-09-23 (list of editions) and 2026-01-13 (Melbourne 1956); the evidence says so.

rounds.scope: All 55 cards: every host city against Olympedia's editions tables, the English Wikipedia list of host cities and a SPARQL query of the edition items; notes; Wikidata checks spot-checked through the API.
rounds.summary: No wrong facts. One documentation error (round 0 claimed a check on Q2182804's alias "Squaw Valley" that did not exist) and two suggestions on the 2018 Swedish note and the Swedish Oslo check. All three verified against the Wikidata API (query 17) and applied.

findings.issue: Round 0 says the checks include the alias "Squaw Valley" of Q2182804 (the preferred P276), but there was no such check, so the back text was never tied to the item the P276 check verifies.
findings.resolution: Verified: Q2182804 has en aliases "Squaw Valley Ski Resort", "Squaw Valley Alpine Meadows" and "Squaw Valley". Added the check Q2182804 en = "Squaw Valley", which makes the round 0 log true, and listed the aliases in the evidence.

findings.issue: The Swedish note left out that Pyeongchang is a county, the disambiguation the English note gives.
findings.resolution: Verified against the Swedish Wikipedia article "Pyeongchang" ("en landskommun (gun) i provinsen Gangwon i Sydkorea") and Q188624's sv alias "Pyeongchang-gun". The reviewer's "härad" is not the Swedish Wikipedia's term, so the note uses "landskommun (gun)": sv "Landskommunen (gun) Pyeongchang i provinsen Gangwon i Sydkorea; IOK skriver PyeongChang 2018."; en made parallel, "Pyeongchang County in Gangwon Province, South Korea; …". The Swedish article was added to the evidence.

findings.issue: The Swedish "Oslo" checks pass only through Q585's multilingual label, and the P131 chain ends at Oslo Municipality (Q5245991), not at Q585, whose labels are checked.
findings.resolution: Verified: Q585 has only en and mul labels; Q5245991 has P36 (capital) Q585 and Q585 has P1376 (capital of) Q5245991. Added the check Q5245991 P36 = Q585, which links the chain to the labelled item, and the evidence now says that the Swedish "Oslo" is the mul label.

findings.issue: The Swedish description calls the 1906 Intercalated Games "mellanspelen 1906", a literal translation; Swedish sources say "extraspelen".
findings.resolution: Verified: the Swedish Wikipedia article "Olympiska sommarspelen 1906" (query 20) begins "Olympiska sommarspelen 1906 eller Extraspelen i Aten 1906". description.sv now says "extraspelen i Aten 1906". No other Swedish text names the 1906 Games.

findings.issue: The last sentence of the Swedish description has no subject ("Hämtad från …"), and "de delade spelen 2026" can read as "the divided Games".
findings.resolution: Reworded: "… båda städerna för spelen 2026, som hade två värdstäder, … Uppgifterna är hämtade från Wikidata och kontrollerade mot …".

findings.issue: The Swedish description uses straight English quotation marks.
findings.resolution: description.sv now uses the Swedish ”Olympiska sommarspelen 1912”.

findings.issue: The Swedish note ("Uppskjutna …: hölls …, fortfarande som Tokyo 2020") is a literal translation without a subject to agree with.
findings.resolution: sv: "Sköts upp ett år på grund av covid-19-pandemin och hölls i juli–augusti 2021, men fortfarande under namnet Tokyo 2020."; en made parallel: "Postponed by a year because of the COVID-19 pandemic and held in July–August 2021, still under the name Tokyo 2020."

rounds.scope: All 55 cards' evidence, every source's licence, the method, the queries and the licensing statement.
rounds.summary: Licensing sound (Wikidata CC0 the only content source; deck CC0). Three warnings (IOC licence evidence quoted only the footer; query 9 recorded as templates; the 1956 quarantine reason misattributed in the licensing text) and five suggestions; all verified and applied.

findings.issue: The olympics-com licenseEvidence quoted only the footer; the terms page was never fetched or quoted.
findings.resolution: Fetched the Internet Archive capture of the terms of service (query 19) and quoted its IP and no-copying clauses verbatim in licenseEvidence. Verification only, as before.

findings.issue: Query 9 (fetch_games.py) was recorded only as URL templates with placeholders.
findings.resolution: Replaced with the exact URLs the script requested, taken from its saved output (2 Wikidata calls listing all 55 ids, 3 Swedish and 3 English Wikipedia calls listing every title).

findings.issue: The quarantine reason was cited only from the all-rights-reserved IOC page, and the licensing text claimed the verification sources only confirmed Wikidata facts; Wikidata's equestrian qualifiers on the Stockholm location were not cited.
findings.resolution: Verified (query 17): Q8411's Stockholm P276 has P641 equestrian sport (Q902378) and P585/P580/P582 June 1956; cited in the evidence. Added the English Wikipedia sentence "The Olympic equestrian events could not be held in Melbourne due to Australia's strict quarantine regulations …" as evidence. The licensing text now says the verification sources supplied, as facts restated in the compiler's words, the reasons in two notes.

findings.issue: The note's cause was backed only by the English Wikipedia, though Wikidata records it.
findings.resolution: Verified (queries 17-18) and added to the Wikidata evidence: P580 2020-07-23 deprecated with reason rescheduling (Q64445414) and P805 Q87805617 "impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the 2020 Summer Olympics"; P580 2021-07-24 with P805 Q87805617.

findings.issue: The note says "Torino in Italian" but the evidence cited only the mul label.
findings.resolution: Verified: Q495 has the it label "Torino" (query 17). Cited in the evidence and added the check Q495 it = "Torino" (the builder would also accept the mul label, which is "Torino" too; the API fetch confirms the it label itself).

findings.issue: The evidence said P276 lists venues "among them" Bislett Stadion, though it is the only one, and did not state how Oslo Municipality relates to Oslo.
findings.resolution: Reworded to "P276 is only the venue Bislett Stadion"; the evidence states Q5245991 P36 Q585 and Q585 P1376 Q5245991, and the check Q5245991 P36 = Q585 was added (see round 1).

findings.issue: The report quotes Wikipedia without pinned revisions or article URLs, does not state the quotations' licence, and quotes a long IOC sentence.
findings.resolution: Every Wikipedia quote was re-fetched with its revision id (query 21; all 62 still verbatim) and each locator now gives the article URL with oldid. The licensing text now says the quotations stay under their sources' licences (Wikipedia CC BY-SA 4.0 by Wikipedia contributors; IOC all rights reserved) and are not part of the CC0 deck. The IOC quote was shortened to "to avoid the problem of quarantine for horses entering Australia". The sources' general URLs were kept, since they name the source as a whole.

findings.issue: Queries 3-7 cite query files q2.rq-q6.rq, numbered one lower; query 14 fetched Wikipedia licence pages under the source "wikidata".
findings.resolution: The commands are kept verbatim (they are what was run) and each purpose now notes the file-name mapping. Query 14 was split into one entry per source (14 Wikidata, 15 English Wikipedia, 16 Swedish Wikipedia); the IOC terms fetch is query 19.

rounds.summary: No factual errors found. Two warnings (six cards still described a single P276 venue as "among them"; method step 1 said independent AI reviewers "may add later" rounds although three had been done) and two suggestions (the quote count 62 vs 64; thin evidence for the 1924 note). All four verified and fixed.

findings.issue: The Wikidata evidence said P276 "gives venues, not the city, among them X" though X is the only P276 value; round 3 had fixed the same wording only on winter-1952.
findings.resolution: Verified with wbgetentities (query 22): Q8456, Q8470, Q9636, Q9646, Q9660 and Q9664 each have exactly one P276 statement (normal rank), the venue named. Reworded to "P276 (location) is only the venue X" on these six cards. The same query showed that the other six venue-only Games (winter-1984, 1994, 2002, 2006, 2010, 2018) have 8 to 13 venues each, so "among them" is correct there and was kept.

findings.issue: Method step 1 said independent AI reviewers "may add later quality-control rounds", though three such rounds had been done and applied.
findings.resolution: Method step 1 now says the deck was cross-checked by independent AI reviewers (rounds 1–4, lenses named) whose findings were verified and applied, and by machine checks against live Wikidata and the SHACL/DCAT-AP validators; the sentence that no human subject expert has reviewed the cards is kept.

findings.issue: Method step 6 and the round 3 log said "all 62 quotes", but the dossier holds 64 Wikipedia quotes (56 Swedish, 8 English).
findings.resolution: Counted: 56 wikipedia-sv and 8 wikipedia-en evidence quotes. Re-fetched every linked revision with action=parse&oldid (query 24, 63 distinct revisions) and confirmed all 64 quotes verbatim. Method step 6 and the purpose of query 21 now say that revids.py checked 62 and the Pyeongchang and 1956 quarantine quotes were checked against their own revisions, 64 in all, and record the round 4 re-check. The round 3 entry is kept as it was written.

findings.issue: The note "The commune's official name is Chamonix-Mont-Blanc" was backed only by Q83236's English label and description, neither of which states an official name, and method step 9 claimed an English Wikipedia check the card did not have.
findings.resolution: Verified (query 22): Q83236 P1448 (official name) is "Chamonix-Mont-Blanc"@fr with preferred rank and "Chamonix"@fr with normal rank. Cited in the Wikidata evidence and added the check Q83236 P1448 = "Chamonix-Mont-Blanc" (the truthy value is the preferred one). Added the English Wikipedia introduction of Chamonix (revision 1376714840, query 23: "Chamonix-Mont-Blanc … more commonly known simply as Chamonix … is a commune …") as a second source; the wikipedia-en source title and use, and method step 9, now include it.

rounds.summary: All 55 host cities, notes, Swedish names and language tags were re-checked, and every builder check was re-run against live Wikidata; no factual errors were found and all round 4 fixes were confirmed in place. One language suggestion (winter-1960, "skidorten" for the ski resort) was verified and fixed.

findings.issue: The Swedish note called Palisades Tahoe "skidorten". A skidort is a place or town people go to for skiing, so the sentence read as if it named the same place twice; Palisades Tahoe is the ski resort (a facility) in the community of Olympic Valley, as the English note says.
findings.resolution: Verified: Wikidata Q2182804 is described as "ski resort in Placer County, California" and Q822230 (Olympic Valley) as an unincorporated community; English Wikipedia "Palisades Tahoe" calls it a ski resort located in Olympic Valley. Swedish "skidanläggning" names the facility. backNote.sv now reads "I Kalifornien. Orten heter i dag Olympic Valley och skidanläggningen Palisades Tahoe."
